newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian wine exports hit record A$508 mln.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian wine exports hit record A$508 mln.

text.p: Australian winemakers exported a record A$507.9 million of wine in the 12 months to August 1996, up 34 percent on the previous corresponding period, Australian Wine Export Council chairman John Keniry said.
Keniry said volume growth was up by 24.7 percent to 138.6 million litres, with the export charge continuing to be driven by the United Kingdom, United States, Canada and New Zealand.
"It is also pleasing that the average price per litre has also increased by 7.7 percent," he said in a statement.

Keniry said bottled red wine exports had grown 37.8 percent to 50.5 million litres, with their value up 46.6 percent to A$229 million. Bottled white wine exports increased 27.1 percent to 52 million litres, earning A$205 million for the 12 months, up 29.2 percent on the previous corresponding period, he said.

The Winemakers Federation of Australia said in the statement this outstanding performance indicated the industry had overcome the poor 1995 vintage and was within reach of its A$1 billion export target for early in the new century.
Chief executive Ian Sutton said the record 1996 vintage of 885,000 tonnes contained 496,000 tonnes of premium fruit.

"Premium stocks have now been replenished and whilst premium red wine demand continues to outstrip supply, winemakers will be looking to shift substantial stocks of white wine into export markets, in order to reduce their stock levels in anticipation of a large 1997 premium vintage and a significant easing of grape prices," he said.
